import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.64

by A. K. Rumyantsev, D. M. Smirnov

Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

A quasiidentity in the language of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \; \bigl((u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v\bigr),$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (for $k = 0$ this
is an identity). A set $\Sigma$ of quasiidentities is a *basis of quasiidentities* of a class
$\mathscr{K}$ of groups if a group satisfies $\Sigma$ exactly when it satisfies every
quasiidentity that holds in all members of $\mathscr{K}$, i.e. $\Sigma$ axiomatizes (modulo the
group axioms) the quasivariety generated by $\mathscr{K}$. The basis $\Sigma$ is *independent* if
no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence (modulo the group axioms) of the remaining members.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

/--
A quasiidentity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$(u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v,$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. Whether a group
satisfies such a formula depends only on the classes of these words modulo the group axioms, so
the words are represented as elements of the free group on `Fin n`. The case $k = 0$ (no premises)
gives the identities.
-/
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, as pairs of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

namespace Quasiidentity

/--
A group `G` satisfies the quasiidentity `q` if for every assignment `x` of the variables in `G`
under which all the premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q` holds. Words are evaluated at `x`
by the homomorphism `FreeGroup.lift x`.
-/
def Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/-- A group `G` satisfies a set `S` of quasiidentities if it satisfies every member of `S`. -/
def SetHolds (S : Set Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds G

/--
The quasiidentity `q` is a consequence of the set `S` of quasiidentities (modulo the group
axioms): every group satisfying `S` satisfies `q`.
-/
def Follows (S : Set Quasiidentity) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G → q.Holds G

/--
A set `S` of quasiidentities is independent if no member of `S` is a consequence of the
remaining members of `S`.
-/
def Independent (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Follows (S \ {q}) q

/--
The quasiidentity `q` holds in the class `𝒦` of groups if every group in `𝒦` satisfies `q`.
-/
def HoldsInClass (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G → q.Holds G

/--
A set `S` of quasiidentities is a basis of quasiidentities of the class `𝒦` of groups if a group
satisfies `S` exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity that holds in the class `𝒦`.
Equivalently, `S` consists of quasiidentities holding in `𝒦` and every quasiidentity holding in
`𝒦` is a consequence of `S`.
-/
def IsBasis (𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop) (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SetHolds S G ↔ ∀ q, HoldsInClass 𝒦 q → q.Holds G

/-- The commutative law $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$, an identity (a quasiidentity with no premises). -/
def commLaw : Quasiidentity where
  numVars := 2
  premises := []
  conclusion := (.of 0 * .of 1, .of 1 * .of 0)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem commLaw_holds (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : commLaw.Holds G := by
  intro x _
  simp [commLaw, mul_comm]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_commLaw_holds_equiv_perm_fin_three : ¬ commLaw.Holds (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) := by
  intro h
  have := h ![Equiv.swap 0 1, Equiv.swap 1 2] (by simp [commLaw])
  simp [commLaw] at this
  exact absurd (congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe this) 0) (by decide)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem Follows.of_mem {S : Set Quasiidentity} {q : Quasiidentity} (hq : q ∈ S) : Follows S q :=
  fun _ _ hS => hS q hq

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem independent_empty : Independent ∅ := by
  simp [Independent]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBasis.holdsInClass {𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop} {S : Set Quasiidentity}
    (hS : IsBasis 𝒦 S) {q : Quasiidentity} (hq : q ∈ S) : HoldsInClass 𝒦 q :=
  fun G _ hG => (hS G).2 (fun _ hq' => hq' G hG) q hq

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBasis.follows {𝒦 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop} {S : Set Quasiidentity}
    (hS : IsBasis 𝒦 S) {q : Quasiidentity} (hq : HoldsInClass 𝒦 q) : Follows S q :=
  fun G _ hG => (hS G).1 hG q hq

end Quasiidentity

open Quasiidentity in
/--
Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

That is, is there a set $\Sigma$ of quasiidentities in the language of groups such that
a group satisfies $\Sigma$ exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity holding in all finite

members of $\Sigma$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.64» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ S : Set Quasiidentity, IsBasis (fun G _ => Finite G) S ∧ Independent S := by

namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

/-- A quasiidentity in the language of groups: a finite conjunction of equations
between group words implies one equation. -/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number of universally quantified variables. -/
  arity : ℕ
  /-- The equations in the antecedent. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin arity) × FreeGroup (Fin arity))
  /-- The equation in the consequent. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin arity) × FreeGroup (Fin arity)

/-- A group satisfies a quasiidentity if every valuation satisfying all its
premises also satisfies its conclusion. -/
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Satisfies (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ valuation : Fin q.arity → G,
    (∀ equation ∈ q.premises,
      FreeGroup.lift valuation equation.1 = FreeGroup.lift valuation equation.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift valuation q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift valuation q.conclusion.2

/-- A set of quasiidentities is a basis for the quasiidentities of all finite
groups if its group models are exactly the groups satisfying every
quasiidentity valid in all finite groups. -/
def IsBasis (T : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
    (∀ q ∈ T, q.Satisfies G) ↔
      ∀ q : GroupQuasiIdentity,
        (∀ (F : Type) [Group F] [Finite F], q.Satisfies F) → q.Satisfies G

/-- A set of group quasiidentities is independent if, for each member, some
group satisfies every other member but not that member. Thus no member is a
semantic consequence of the others modulo the group axioms. -/
def IsIndependent (T : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
    (∀ r ∈ T, r ≠ q → r.Satisfies G) ∧ ¬q.Satisfies G

/--
Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of
quasiidentities? That is, is there an independent set of universal Horn
sentences in the language of groups whose group models are exactly the groups
satisfying every quasiidentity valid in every finite group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.64» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ T : Set GroupQuasiIdentity, IsBasis T ∧ IsIndependent T := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.64»

Represented a quasiidentity as a finite list of premise equations implying one conclusion equation; the empty premise list includes ordinary identities.
Expressed being a basis semantically: a group satisfies the proposed set exactly when it satisfies every quasiidentity valid in every finite group.
Expressed independence as semantic nonconsequence modulo the group axioms: for each member there is a group satisfying all other members and falsifying that member.

`FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. All consequence relations below are taken modulo the group axioms, i.e.

generated by $\mathfrak{K}$ within the class of all groups). The set $\Sigma$ is *independent*
if no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence of the remaining members.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

/-- A quasiidentity in the language of groups, with variables indexed by `ℕ`: a finite set
of premises $s_i = t_i$ and a conclusion $u = v$, where all $s_i, t_i, u, v$ are group words,
represented as elements of `FreeGroup ℕ`. It stands for the universal Horn sentence
$\forall \bar x\ (\bigwedge_i s_i = t_i \to u = v)$. Identities are the quasiidentities with
no premises. -/
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The premises $s_i = t_i$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `G` satisfies the quasiidentity `q` if for every assignment of the variables in
`G` (equivalently, every homomorphism `f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`) validating all premises of
`q`, the conclusion of `q` holds. -/
def Quasiidentity.Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, f p.1 = f p.2) → f q.conclusion.1 = f q.conclusion.2

/-- The quasiidentities of a class `K` of groups: those holding in every group in `K`. -/
def quasiidentitiesOf (K : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Set Quasiidentity :=
  {q | ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], K G → q.Holds G}

/-- A set `S` of quasiidentities is a *basis of quasiidentities* of a class `K` of groups if
a group satisfies all quasiidentities of `K` if and only if it satisfies all members of `S`;
that is, `S` axiomatizes (modulo the group axioms) the quasivariety generated by `K`. -/
def IsQuasiidentityBasis (K : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ q ∈ quasiidentitiesOf K, q.Holds G) ↔ ∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds G

/-- A set `S` of quasiidentities is *independent* if no member of `S` is a consequence
(modulo the group axioms) of the remaining members: for every `q ∈ S` there is a group
satisfying every member of `S` other than `q` but not `q`. -/
def IsIndependent (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), (∀ q' ∈ S, q' ≠ q → q'.Holds G) ∧ ¬ q.Holds G

/-- The quasiidentities of a class of groups form a basis of quasiidentities of that class. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem isQuasiidentityBasis_quasiidentitiesOf (K : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) :
    IsQuasiidentityBasis K (quasiidentitiesOf K) := fun _ _ => Iff.rfl

/-- The empty set of quasiidentities is independent. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem isIndependent_empty : IsIndependent ∅ := fun _ h => h.elim

/-- A quasiidentity whose conclusion is trivial holds in every group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem Quasiidentity.holds_of_conclusion_eq (P : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ))

    Quasiidentity.Holds ⟨P, (w, w)⟩ G := fun _ _ => rfl

/-- The trivial group satisfies every quasiidentity. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem Quasiidentity.holds_unit (q : Quasiidentity) : q.Holds Unit := fun _ _ => rfl

/-- The identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in a group `G` if and only if `G` is commutative. -/

theorem Quasiidentity.holds_comm_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :

The single-slot decomposition and its notes (basis = axiomatization of the quasivariety generated by finite groups modulo the group axioms; independence = no member follows from the rest modulo the group axioms; `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ Σ, ...`) match the standard meaning of the question and are followed exactly.
modeling_decisions: Group words are represented by elements of `FreeGroup ℕ` rather than raw terms of the first-order language {·, ⁻¹, 1}. Values of terms in any group depend only on their image in the free group, and every free-group element is the image of a term, so satisfaction predicates on groups coincide; the existence of an independent basis is invariant under this identification (an independent set contains no two logically equivalent members, so the passage between the two presentations is injective on independent sets).

Variables are indexed by ℕ (countably many), and an assignment is a homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`; a quasiidentity mentions only finitely many variables, and unused variables are harmless since groups are nonempty.

Premises form a `Finset` (finite conjunction, unordered), and the conclusion is a single equation; identities are the case of empty premises (standard: identities count as quasiidentities). Allowing/disallowing empty premises does not affect the answer since `x = x` may be added as a premise.

Consequence and the basis condition are taken relative to the class of all groups (modulo the group axioms), as is standard for 'basis of quasiidentities of a class of groups' (Gorbunov; Budkin) and as specified in the decomposition notes.

The class of finite groups is `fun (G : Type) [Group G] => Finite G` and all groups quantified over live in `Type` (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files. # Conjecture 8.64

by A. K. Rumyantsev, D. M. Smirnov

Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

/-- A quasiidentity in the language of groups consists of finitely many universally quantified
variables, a finite conjunction of equations between group terms, and one concluding equation. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  arity : ℕ
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin arity) × FreeGroup (Fin arity))
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin arity) × FreeGroup (Fin arity)

/-- A group satisfies a quasiidentity if every valuation satisfying all its premise equations also
satisfies its concluding equation. -/
def QuasiIdentity.HoldsIn (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Fin q.arity → G,
    (∀ e ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift v e.1 = FreeGroup.lift v e.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift v q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift v q.conclusion.2

/-- A quasiidentity is valid in all finite groups if every finite group satisfies it. -/
def QuasiIdentity.ValidInFiniteGroups (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], q.HoldsIn G

/-- A set of quasiidentities is a basis for the quasiidentities of all finite groups if, among
groups, its models are exactly the groups satisfying every quasiidentity valid in all finite
groups. -/
def IsBasisForFiniteGroups (basis : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
    (∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.ValidInFiniteGroups → q.HoldsIn G) ↔
      ∀ q ∈ basis, q.HoldsIn G

/-- A set of quasiidentities is independent modulo the group axioms if none of its members holds in
every group satisfying all the other members. -/
def IsIndependent (basis : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ basis, ¬∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
    (∀ r ∈ basis, r ≠ q → r.HoldsIn G) → q.HoldsIn G

/--
Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

Here a basis axiomatizes, in the presence of the group axioms, exactly the groups satisfying every
quasiidentity true in every finite group. Independence means that no member of the basis follows
from the remaining members modulo the group axioms.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.64» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ basis : Set QuasiIdentity,
      IsBasisForFiniteGroups basis ∧ IsIndependent basis := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.64»

/-!
# Conjecture 8.64

by A. K. Rumyantsev, D. M. Smirnov

Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

A *quasiidentity* in the language of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall \bar x \; \bigl(w_1(\bar x) = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k(\bar x) = 1 \bigr)
\to w(\bar x) = 1,$$
where $w_1, \dots, w_k, w$ are group words in finitely many variables (an equation
$t = s$ between group words is written as $t s^{-1} = 1$). A set $\Sigma$ of
quasiidentities is a *basis of quasiidentities* of a class $\mathcal{K}$ of groups if
the quasiidentities true in every group of $\mathcal{K}$ are exactly the consequences
of $\Sigma$ (modulo the group axioms); equivalently, the quasivariety of groups defined
by $\Sigma$ is the quasivariety generated by $\mathcal{K}$. A basis $\Sigma$ is
*independent* if no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence of the remaining members of
$\Sigma$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.64»

/-- A quasiidentity in the language of groups: a universal Horn sentence
$\forall \bar x \; (w_1(\bar x) = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k(\bar x) = 1) \to w(\bar x) = 1$
with finitely many premises `w₁ = 1, …, wₖ = 1` and one conclusion `w = 1`.

Group words are elements of the free group on the countable set `ℕ` of variables. Every word
involves only finitely many variables and there are finitely many premises, so each
quasiidentity involves only finitely many variables. Since the group language has inverses,
an equation `t = s` between group words is expressed as `t * s⁻¹ = 1`. The case of no
premises is allowed, so identities are quasiidentities. -/
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The words `w₁, …, wₖ` of the premises `w₁ = 1, …, wₖ = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

namespace Quasiidentity

/-- `q.Holds G` means that the quasiidentity `q` holds in the group `G`: for every assignment
`x : ℕ → G` of the variables for which all premises evaluate to `1`, the conclusion also
evaluates to `1`. -/
def Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → G, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1) → FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion = 1

/-- `q.HoldsInFiniteGroups` means that the quasiidentity `q` holds in every finite group. -/
def HoldsInFiniteGroups (q : Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], q.Holds G

/-- The identity `x₀ x₁ x₀⁻¹ x₁⁻¹ = 1` (a quasiidentity with no premises) holds in every
commutative group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem holds_commutator_of_isMulCommutative (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulCommutative G] :
    (Quasiidentity.mk ∅
      (FreeGroup.of 0 * FreeGroup.of 1 * (FreeGroup.of 0)⁻¹ * (FreeGroup.of 1)⁻¹)).Holds G := by
  intro x _
  simp [mul_assoc]

/-- The quasiidentity `x₀ ^ 2 = 1 → x₀ = 1` does not hold in every finite group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_holdsInFiniteGroups_sq :
    ¬ (Quasiidentity.mk {FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2} (FreeGroup.of 0)).HoldsInFiniteGroups := by
  intro h
  have := h (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) (fun _ => Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (by
    intro w hw
    simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hw
    subst hw
    decide)
  simp at this

end Quasiidentity

/-- A set `S` of quasiidentities is a basis of quasiidentities of the class of all finite
groups: the quasiidentities true in every finite group are exactly the consequences of `S`
modulo the group axioms. Semantically, a group satisfies every member of `S` if and only if it
satisfies every quasiidentity that holds in every finite group; that is, the quasivariety of
groups defined by `S` is the quasivariety generated by the finite groups. -/
def IsQuasiidentityBasisOfFiniteGroups (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
    (∀ q ∈ S, q.Holds G) ↔ ∀ q : Quasiidentity, q.HoldsInFiniteGroups → q.Holds G

/-- A set `S` of quasiidentities is independent if no member of `S` is a consequence (modulo the
group axioms) of the remaining members of `S`: for every `q ∈ S` there is a group satisfying all
members of `S` other than `q` but not `q`. -/
def IsIndependent (S : Set Quasiidentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ S, ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), (∀ q' ∈ S, q' ≠ q → q'.Holds G) ∧ ¬ q.Holds G

/--
Does the class of all finite groups possess an independent basis of quasiidentities?

That is, is there a set $\Sigma$ of quasiidentities in the language of groups such that

* a group satisfies all members of $\Sigma$ if and only if it satisfies every quasiidentity
  that holds in all finite groups (so $\Sigma$ is a basis of quasiidentities of the class of
  finite groups, modulo the group axioms), and
* no member of $\Sigma$ is a consequence of the remaining members of $\Sigma$ (so $\Sigma$ is
  independent)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.64» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ S : Set Quasiidentity, IsQuasiidentityBasisOfFiniteGroups S ∧ IsIndependent S := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.64»
